question: Why did the error rate go up on 16 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment of checkout v4.18 to us-east caused increased error rate in service catalog.
why_chain: Checkout v4.18 deployment to us-east introduced a new version of the service.
The new version of the service caused issues with the upstream catalog-db.
The issues with catalog-db led to timeout errors in the service catalog.
The timeout errors increased the error rate in the service catalog.
The increased error rate is observed on 16 March 2026.

contributing_factors.description: Increased request volume to service catalog caused higher error rate.
why_chain: The error rate in service catalog increased from 0.36% to 4.12%.
The increase in error rate coincides with a 24% increase in request volume.
The increase in request volume is likely due to a campaign or user behavior change.
The campaign or user behavior change led to more users or requests than usual.
The increased load on the service catalog caused the error rate to rise.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Configuration change to service catalog caused the error rate to increase.
ruled_out.reason: No configuration change was observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: Data quality issues caused the error rate to increase.
ruled_out.reason: No data quality issues were observed in the evidence.

ruled_out.hypothesis: External dependency issues caused the error rate to increase.
ruled_out.reason: No external dependency issues were observed in the evidence.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service catalog rose from 0.36% to 4.12% (+1044%), with a change point at 2026-03-16T09:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service catalog: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.13).
At the same time, request volume for service catalog stayed about the same (1617 per 5 min before, 2010 per 5 min after, +24%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service catalog rose (121 ms before, 217 ms after, +80%).
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, ap-south; 14 min after the change; record R011; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, us-east; 20 min after the change; record R012; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
catalog-db status page: investigating degraded performance (catalog; 30 min after the change; record R014; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
catalog: ERROR upstream catalog-db timeout after 3 retries (catalog, eu-west; 24 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed checkout v4.18 to us-east (routine release) (checkout, us-east; 225 min before the change; record R010; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 225 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✓ 3 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Rollback the checkout v4.18 deployment to us-east.
Monitor the service catalog for any further issues and take corrective action if needed.
Review and optimize the service catalog's request handling to better manage increased load.
